why: B answered with two of its four metrics. `preorg_rmsd` and `ligand_rmsf` are there and look fine; `rotamer_entropy` came back null and `induced_fit_risk` is absent entirely, which is what a stream serving a half-initialised checkpoint does -- the weights load, the forward pass runs, and some heads are not there. Nothing about the exit status or the `result` says so, and a consumer reading `metrics.get('induced_fit_risk', 0.0)` would read the riskiest possible design as the safest, since 0.15 is this metric's floor and 0.0 is below it. `metrics_reported` requires each named metric to be a FINITE NUMBER, so it catches the null as well as the absence -- which is why the gate reads the three raw quantities plus the derived scalar rather than trusting the payload's key set.
